newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa says NatMut to add 291 mln Ffr to 96 income.
newsitem.headline: Axa says NatMut to add 291 mln Ffr to 96 income.

text.p: French insurer Axa said on Friday its unit Australian insurer National Mutual Holdings would contribute 291 million francs to its 1996 net income, up from a pro forma 1995 contribution of 125 million francs.
"The contribution of National Mutual Holdings, 51 per cent held by Axa, to Axa's full-year 1996 net income (net of minority interests) amounts to 291 million francs," it said in a statement.
"This compares very favourably with the pro forma contribution for 1995, which amounted to 125 million."
Axa said that the actual contribution for 1995, consolidated for one month only, was three million francs.

Axa said the 1996 improvement was driven by cost-cutting and improved policyholder retention in Australia and New Zealand, business growth in Hong Kong, more favourable financial markets in 1996 and positive currency fluctuations.

National Mutual reported last month consolidated net income of A$210.9 million for its full year to September 30, 1996. This worked out at 865 million francs based on an exchange rate of 4.10 francs per A$1.00 as of September 30, 1996.
For Axa's financial statements, National Mutual Holdings accounts are consolidated under US GAAP principles.
